edges.description: Reduced EEFSEC function lowers cellular selenoprotein levels.
Selenoprotein deficiency manifests clinically as progressive neurodegeneration with cerebellar pathology.
Early-onset selenoprotein-related neurodegeneration leads to global developmental delay.
Central nervous system neurodegeneration causes progressive spasticity.
Impaired cerebellar development and neurodegeneration present as cerebellar hypoplasia on brain MRI.
Progressive cerebellar neurodegeneration results in progressive cerebellar atrophy on brain MRI.
Progressive motor impairment with synaptic defects parallels the progressive motor decline of the human disorder.
edges.limitations: RNAi knockdown in an invertebrate is not the biallelic hypomorphic missense genotype of patients, and the abstract reports motor and synaptic readouts only, not the cerebellar hypoplasia and atrophy that define the human neurodegeneration.

nodes.description: EEFSEC/eEFSec is the specialized translation elongation factor that promotes selenocysteine incorporation into selenoproteins. Pathogenic variants impair this elongation-stage Sec-tRNA delivery mechanism.

evidence.reference_title: Crystal structures of the human elongation factor eEFSec suggest a non-canonical mechanism for selenocysteine incorporation.
evidence.snippet: A specialized translation elongation factor, eEFSec in eukaryotes and SelB in prokaryotes, promotes selenocysteine incorporation into selenoproteins by a still poorly understood mechanism.
